blockers.likely_cause: Confirmed by probe: the sun fixer's near-sun sky cap (kSkySunCap 10, past white, applied in camSkyRolloff(lin, d)) feeds the camera meter's guards. TargetExposureLog2 (PhotoCamera.cpp 298-334) pulls exposure toward kHighlightLimit on the kMeterHighlight percentile and toward kSkyTopLimit on the sky's bright end. The glow of a sun at or just past the frame edge now meters several times brighter, so the whole frame drops. The sun fixer never shot woods_pine2_evening. Its own build already showed the smaller drops in lowsun_fp and pine_rays. Root fix: the meter should read the sky at the plain roll-off cap, or leave the glow's extra light out of the highlight and sky-top readings, or exclude blocks within the glow radius whether the sun is in frame or just outside it.

AI link review: AI sight is now simulation. SimulateFogSight runs at the end of World::SimulateLandscape (WorldSetup.cpp 1326), before PerformAI (World.cpp 682 before 1729). It uses ComputeFogMedium(WorldFogInputs(land), tuning, true), the same function and inputs the renderer uses, which adds only aridity (not an AI term). The AI terms do not read viewDistance or the fog range. The renderer no longer calls SetFogSight; only TerrainLighting.cpp does. Target.cpp 636-646 is unchanged. The inputs are deterministic from synced weather, date and heights, except the per-machine knobs fogDensity and fogMist. It is thread-safe today because BACKGROUND_AI is 0 and everything runs on the main thread. FogSightMedium() returns a reference into a static, which would race if AI moved to a worker thread.

AI link test gap: tests 376, 421 and 463 pin the pure helpers (AI medium equals the drawn medium across the knobs; invariant under post off, interior and render-only knobs; renderer-free map equals the horizon map). Case 421 cannot fail, because UpdateFogSightMedium never receives gate state. Nothing pins that the renderer cannot call SetFogSight, that SimulateFogSight runs before PerformAI, or what WorldFogInputs reads. A source contract test would close this.

Owner call (from the fixer, kept): in classic lighting, or with volFog off, AI still takes the mist that the screen does not draw. Also, a day's setFog is now drawn at 0.75 of the classic extinction while AI's weather part stays the classic tactical fog, so about a fifth of a surface is still drawn at the AI's tactical end.
Cost: the machine was busy, so the raw means cannot be compared with round 3. Treat the cost as provisional until a quiet re-time; see cost_summary.
cost_summary: There is no measurable cost growth over rounds 2 and 3, but the machine was not quiet. I ran run-timing.ps1 from the look-director engine root against dist/look-director-rwdi on junction RemasterUD-look-director-timing, using round 3's split tests (renamed crit4t_*, same views, clocks and interleaved tip/overhaul order). It ran as 4 background runs, checked at least every 3 minutes. 170 of 179 GPU samples had a foreign PoseidonGame (up to 4 at once during the first part: look-puddle, look_shine, look_probe and van_* runs). Round 3 had 0 of 142. Because of that, the raw mean delta of +1.94 ms against round 3's +1.45 ms over 21 views is not a cost result. Usable estimate: take each shot's minimum GPU frame and keep the 14 views whose tip minimum matched round 3 within 0.5 ms. On those the overhaul delta is +1.56 ms against round 3's +1.54 ms, and the overhaul minimum frame averages 10.46 ms against 10.37 ms. Every one of those views is within 0.2 ms except sinai_desert_noon (+3.59 against +1.70), and that one is noise: its two overhaul samples differ by 3 ms within one run with a foreign game running. Seven contended views cannot be compared: noon_fields, lowsun_fp, forest_edge_golden, sunrise_ridge, woods_pine2_evening, dawn_valley, town_fog_night. Static check: the five round 4 patches add no texture reads, draw calls or passes, only ALU work plus a per-step 64x64 height hash on the CPU. The AI sight map build (about 150 ms) now runs on the main thread at island load. A quiet-machine re-time is still needed for a formal number.
